dishes.name: Copilot Fusion Fusilli
dishes.tag: A little help from the whole kitchen
dishes.description: Explore model routing, then build something with agents.

practice.intro: Try these prompts in the Copilot conversation beside the diner. Select Copilot Fusion in the app's model picker if it is available; other models can do the exercise too, but that does not demonstrate Fusion routing. Use the app's routing information as evidence, not a model's guess. No repository or editor is needed.

prompts.label: Explore routing
prompts.text: Explain Copilot Fusion's single, cascade, and critique patterns with a diner analogy. Compare an explanation task, a small code change, and a design task. Distinguish documented behavior from suggestions. Link official sources, and do not claim which models handled this request unless the app exposes that evidence. Stay in this conversation; do not modify files or create resources.

prompts.label: Build a small function
prompts.text: In this conversation, write a pure Python function normalize_ticket(text: str) -> str | None for our diner. Accept only fusilli, fried-chicken, soup, dip, and sandwich. Ignore letter case and outer whitespace; normalize runs of whitespace or underscores to one hyphen. Reject URLs and unknown dishes. Include focused unittest cases for those rules, including Fried_Chicken and a URL containing fusilli. Keep the code in chat: do not write files, install anything, run commands, or create remote resources. Explain how I can verify the answer; do not claim unrun tests passed.

attendee: Open your fresh repository in Copilot. Start a new chat and select Copilot Fusion.
Ask: Explain single, cascade, and critique. When would each pattern help?
Ask Copilot to build a small diner menu with tests. Inspect the changes and the model-routing information together.
staff: Show routing on a real codebase. Compare a small explanation, a bounded code change, and a design task.
For a blank-prompt demonstration, choose From scratch. Let the audience shape the prompt, then inspect the agent's work rather than treating generation as verification.

dishes.name: Microsoft Copilot SDK Fried Chicken
dishes.tag: Your app. Your tools. One helpful agent.
dishes.description: Give an agent application a custom tool of its own.

practice.intro: Inspect the real bundled starter below, then paste this source-grounded prompt into the Copilot conversation beside the diner. This is a code walkthrough, not a running SDK agent. No editor or dependency installation is needed; executing the optional SDK sample is a separate activity.

prompts.label: Walk through the SDK starter
prompts.text: Walk through the Python Copilot SDK starter included below. Explain define_tool, how create_session exposes the menu tool, and the difference between the application's tool and a chat prompt. Explain the permission implications of PermissionHandler.approve_all. Propose one small menu-tool improvement in chat without modifying files, installing dependencies, running code, or making an SDK request. Clearly distinguish what the source shows from behavior that would need execution to verify.

attendee: Read the bundled main.py below. With a prepared environment, inspect your own starter copy too.
Ask Copilot: What does define_tool do, and how does create_session make get_menu available to the agent?
Propose one menu item or tool extension in Copilot. Running the optional sample separately requires the documented SDK prerequisites and approval; a code walkthrough is not an SDK execution.
staff: Trace the application, session, custom tool, and response. Distinguish application code from a prompt.
Demonstrate a bounded tool change. Discuss authentication and tool permissions before connecting a real external service.

dishes.name: Agentic Alphabet Soup
dishes.tag: Two recipes for getting work done
dishes.description: Agentic Workflows and coding agent, with their different triggers and outputs.
attendee: Open .github/workflows/weekly-workshop-triage.md. Find the trigger, permissions, tools, and safe outputs.
Open the prepared issue and coding agent pull request. Trace the issue request through the agent's changes.
Compare the mechanisms: Agentic Workflows run repository automation from declared triggers; coding agent takes an assigned issue to a proposed pull request. Neither bypasses review.
staff: Walk through the workflow source and its declared safe outputs, then the separate issue-to-PR path. The inherited workflow is a read-only example here; do not dispatch it against the shared source repository.
Show the coding agent's evidence and checks. Do not describe a scheduled workflow as the coding agent or put stacked-PR content in this dish.

dishes.name: Autofix Artichoke Dip
dishes.tag: Review, spot, fix, and taste again
dishes.description: Code Review, CodeQL, Autofix, and AI-powered security remediation.
attendee: Open the prepared Code Review repository. Read Copilot's review on a feature PR and explain one suggested change.
In the security repository, compare the TypeScript CodeQL findings with the PHP AI scanning findings.
Inspect an Autofix suggestion, review the proposed diff, and explain how you would verify the fix before merging.
staff: Keep review, deterministic analysis, AI findings, and remediation distinct. Show the evidence behind each.
Choose Agent-driven remediation for the deeper exercise: trace an assigned security alert to the agent's completed fix PR, then inspect its checks.

dishes.name: GitHub Delivery Club Sandwich
dishes.tag: A satisfying stack of delivery basics
dishes.description: Issue, branch, pull request, Actions checks, merge, and deploy.
attendee: Open your fresh bingo repository and deployed game. Create a small, specific issue describing a change.
Create a branch, implement the change, and open a PR linked to the issue. Inspect the diff and Actions checks.
Review and merge the PR. Follow the Pages deployment and verify the result in the game.
staff: Trace the complete delivery loop, including the distinction between passing checks and human review.
Optional deeper exercise: choose Stacked PRs to review the prepared layers, their base branches, and the order in which they merge.
